title: FedPEFT-IMU — Experimental Results

encoders.name: limu_bert
encoders.pretrained_source: Official LIMU-BERT weights pretrained on HHAR (phones + smartwatches)

encoders.name: ssl_wearables
encoders.pretrained_source: Official Oxford harnet10 weights, self-supervised on UK-Biobank wrist data

encoders.name: unimts
encoders.architecture: ST-GCN, 10 graph blocks over a 22-joint skeleton, 64-512 channels
encoders.pretrained_source: Official UniMTS weights (motion-capture-synthesised IMU aligned with text)

encoders.name: halo
encoders.architecture: Patch-channel Transformer, 8 alternating temporal/channel layers, d=192
encoders.pretrained_source: Our re-implementation, self-supervised (MAE + patch contrastive) on the Capture-24 pool users

methods.name: fedavg_scratch
methods.label: FedAvg from scratch
methods.description: Random initialisation; the whole model is trained and uploaded every round.

methods.name: v0_full_ft
methods.label: V0 · Full fine-tuning
methods.description: Pretrained encoder; the whole model is fine-tuned and uploaded (upper-cost baseline).

methods.name: v1_head_only
methods.label: V1 · Head only
methods.description: Frozen pretrained encoder; only the heads g and h are trained and uploaded (lower-cost baseline).

methods.name: v2_lora_naive
methods.label: V2 · LoRA, naive avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; the server averages A and B separately: avg(B)·avg(A).

methods.name: v3_lora_exact
methods.label: V3 · LoRA, exact avg
methods.description: LoRA (r=8) + heads; exact FedEx-LoRA aggregation avg(B·A), residual folded into W0.

methods.name: v4_hetero_rank
methods.label: V4 · Heterogeneous ranks
methods.description: Device tiers train LoRA ranks 2/4/8; zero-pad, exact aggregation, SVD re-factorisation.

methods.name: v5_proposed
methods.label: V5 · FedPEFT-IMU (proposed)
methods.description: V4 + local norm + local input adapter + personal head + class-prototype alignment.

findings: Against the first run, the class-imbalance fixes change federated macro-F1 by +0.080 on average (per window, 28 models; largest +0.192 for HALO V4). Classes stuck at F1 < 0.01: 35 before, 14 after.
HMM smoothing of each user's window sequence adds +0.054 macro-F1 on average across the federated models (best smoothed result 0.785).

Centralized from scratch, HALO is the strongest architecture (macro-F1 0.599). Starting from the pretrained weights improves every encoder: LIMU-BERT +0.094, ssl-wearables +0.140, UniMTS +0.078, HALO +0.069 macro-F1.

Training from scratch in the federation (non-IID users, 20 % participation) loses LIMU-BERT 0.103, ssl-wearables 0.244, UniMTS 0.170, HALO 0.244 macro-F1 against centralized training from scratch. This is the gap the pretrained encoders are meant to close.

FedPEFT-IMU (V5) against full fine-tuning (V0), macro-F1: LIMU-BERT 0.432 vs 0.394 with 9x less uplink; ssl-wearables 0.720 vs 0.682 with 50x less uplink; UniMTS 0.599 vs 0.587 with 36x less uplink; HALO 0.588 vs 0.560 with 92x less uplink.

Federated LoRA without personalisation (best of V2/V3) against V0: LIMU-BERT V3 0.351 vs V0 0.394; ssl-wearables V2 0.707 vs V0 0.682; UniMTS V2 0.598 vs V0 0.587; HALO V3 0.556 vs V0 0.560. LoRA matches or beats full fine-tuning for ssl-wearables, UniMTS, HALO; for LIMU-BERT the frozen features need more than a low-rank update in this round budget.

Exact LoRA aggregation (V3) versus naive averaging (V2), macro-F1 difference: LIMU-BERT +0.003, ssl-wearables -0.029, UniMTS -0.039, HALO +0.002. In this setting the naive error is small (see the aggregation-error chart) and does not cost accuracy. Exact aggregation must ship the dense residual to every client: downlink per round is LIMU-BERT 2x, ssl-wearables 34x, UniMTS 23x, HALO 10x that of V2.
LoRA rank (ssl-wearables, V3): r=2 0.697, r=4 0.688, r=8 0.678, r=16 0.668. The best rank is r=2 at 0.51 MB per client-round; a larger rank does not buy accuracy here.
Highest worst-10 % client F1 per encoder: LIMU-BERT V5 0.201; ssl-wearables V2 0.462 (V5 0.381); UniMTS V0 0.396 (V5 0.245); HALO V2 0.375 (V5 0.304).

New users, zero-shot (V5 = nearest global prototype; BatchNorm encoders first estimate their norm statistics from the new user's unlabelled windows): LIMU-BERT V5 0.290 vs V3 0.377; ssl-wearables V5 0.562 vs V3 0.615; UniMTS V5 0.526 vs V3 0.549; HALO V5 0.491 vs V3 0.552. The shared classifier of V3 transfers better to brand-new users than V5's prototype rule; V5's advantage is on the devices that trained with it.

For 15 of 28 federated models, 5 minutes of labels score below zero-shot. The models with the weaker half of zero-shot scores gain +0.032 on average from 5 minutes of labels, the stronger half changes by -0.028. The few-shot fit already corrects for its class-balanced sample, so the remaining loss suggests the classifier over-fits the 6-30 windows per class; regularising it towards the global classifier is the next step.
Budget note: UniMTS ran with a reduced compute budget (see the callouts), so compare its methods with each other.
All numbers come from one user split (seed 0). Differences of a few F1 points should be confirmed with the 'full' profile (3 held-out lists) before they are claimed.
